column1: Pour the warm milk into a stand mixer bowl, sprinkle the yeast on top and let it sit 3–4 minutes until frothy.
Mix in the eggs, butter and sugar until combined.
Add the salt and 4 cups of the flour and mix with the paddle just until barely combined. Rest 5 minutes, then switch to the dough hook.
Knead on medium speed 5–7 minutes, adding up to 1/2 cup more flour only if needed. The dough should be smooth but still tacky.
Transfer to a greased bowl, cover and let rise in a warm spot until nearly doubled, about 30 minutes.
Meanwhile mix the soft butter, brown sugar and cinnamon for the filling.
Turn the dough onto a well-floured surface, flour the top and roll into roughly a 24x15 inch rectangle.
Spread the filling evenly over the dough and roll it up tightly from a long side.
Cut into 12 rolls and place in a greased 9x13 inch pan. Cover and let rise 20 minutes while the oven preheats to 375°F (191°C).
Warm the heavy cream just until no longer cold and pour it over the risen rolls.
Bake 22–25 minutes until lightly golden and the center rolls are cooked through, tenting with foil if browning too fast.
For the frosting beat the cream cheese and butter until smooth, then beat in the extract and powdered sugar.
Spread the frosting over the rolls once cooled slightly.
